plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Sell high-beta, low-scoring names (METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to cure the concentration breach and reduce overall exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a realistic ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure, leading to lower expected drawdowns. However, potential upside is also limited.

plan: Trim high-beta names (METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) and leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to reduce overall risk.
Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Buy NVDD at 4% as a strong scanner setup to add quality tech exposure.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF presence.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets a ~2.5%/month return, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces concentration and leverage while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate drawdowns with potential for solid growth.

plan: Add to high-beta names (METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) and leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to increase exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Buy NVDD at 6% as a strong scanner setup, leaning into growth.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to stretch for higher growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for a ~4%/month return, embracing stretch growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration, which amplifies both potential upside and drawdown. Be aware of leveraged ETF decay and the potential for rapid losses with strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all high-beta names (METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) and leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to near zero.
Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Add to QQQI, increasing income exposure for steady distributions.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets a ~1%/month return, focusing on parking cash for yield. It significantly reduces high-beta and leveraged exposure, favoring income-generating ETFs. While aiming for low drawdown and reliable distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are variable.
